text:
alex: FYI I'm seeing intermittent gRPC streaming stalls from model-serving pods in us-west-2a. Long-lived streams (30s+) drop with 'grpc: received unexpected EOF' and the request just hangs until client reconnects. p99 latency spikes.

devon: Any packet-level traces? sounds like fragmentation or MTU.

alex: Attached a short tcpdump snippet from a problematic pod -> node path:
```
15:32:10.123456 IP 10.10.1.45.51820 > 10.10.2.12.60000: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12870, ack 9876, win 29200, length 525
15:32:10.123467 IP (frag 1/2) 10.10.1.45 > 10.10.2.12: ip-proto-UDP 
15:32:10.123478 IP (frag 2/2) 10.10.1.45 > 10.10.2.12: ip-proto-UDP
```
shows IP fragmentation on egress from pod host.

sam: which CNI and overlay MTU are we running?

alex: Cilium with VXLAN encapsulation, cluster default overlay MTU set to 1450 for cloud's 1500. BUT some GPU nodes (SR-IOV) were configured with host MTU 9000 and bypass encapsulation, while others kept 1500. That mismatch means when a pod on 9000-MTU host talks to a pod on a 1500-MTU path, large gRPC frames get fragmented.

maria: Does gRPC handle fragmentation ok normally? usually yes, but streaming + GSO/GRO can combine with PMTU blackhole to make kernel drop or reassemble badly, causing application-level EOFs.

alex: Exactly. We also saw kernel offloads enabled on the SR-IOV NICs (GSO/TX) which makes the host send large skbs that get fragmented in the network stack and sometimes dropped upstream by intermediate devices.

devon: Can we repro with iperf or h2load?

alex: Repro'd with h2load against our internal echo-stream endpoint. When payloads exceed ~12KB we saw stalls. Quick test commands used:
```bash
# from pod namespace
apt-get install -y h2load
h2load -n 1000 -c 10 -m 1 -t 30 --h1 http://echo-service.default.svc.cluster.local/stream
# on host: tcpdump -ni eth0 -w trace.pcap
```

infra-bot: NOTE: eskernel-alert: node gpu-12 reported high tx-err and GRO mismatch at 2026-10-03T15:30:12Z

sam: Any quick mitigations? we need to reduce user impact on production models.

alex: Short term: enabled net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on affected nodes and disabled GSO/TCP segmentation offload on the SR-IOV NICs (ethtool -K <iface> gso off tso off gro off). That immediately reduced EOFs for streams > MTU.

maria: Good call. Longer term we should standardize MTU across all nodes and ensure Cilium encapsulation MTU matches host. Options: move everyone to 9000 (jumbo) or force VXLAN with consistent 1450 on all nodes.

devon: Is there any perf hit when turning off GSO/TSO on GPU nodes? Could affect throughput for bulk transfers.

alex: Some CPU hit for throughput but our samples show <5% increase in CPU for steady traffic; acceptable as temporary fallback. For durable fix we'll either:
- roll out host MTU=9000 on all nodes and set Cilium to use SR-IOV-aware mode
- or force VXLAN non-bypass on SR-IOV nodes so overlay MTU is consistent (probably easier and safer)

sam: Ticketed this and created a rollout plan? link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3421

maria: Also add a preflight check to node provisioning: verify 'ip link show' MTU and CNI MTU match; add to node-exporter metrics.

alex: I've pushed a one-off DaemonSet to toggle off GSO/TCP offload on the 3 impacted SR-IOV nodes and the stream errors have dropped to near zero. Will monitor for 2 hours then schedule a controlled kube-drain upgrade to standardize MTU.

devon: Thanks. For postmortem include pcap, ethtool outputs, node provisioning diffs, and the Cilium config change.

alex: Will do. If anyone sees more hits, ping me @alex and I'll revert the DS quickly. :thumbsup:
